title: Choose Numbers From Two Arrays in Range
summary: Given two 0-indexed integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of the same length, find the number of balanced ranges [l, r] (inclusive) where the sum of the selected elements from nums1 equals the sum of the selected elements from nums2.
statement: Given two 0-indexed integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of the same length, find the number of balanced ranges [l, r] (inclusive) where the sum of the selected elements from nums1 equals the sum of the selected elements from nums2. A range is considered balanced if, for every index i within the range [l, r], either nums1[i] or nums2[i] is chosen such that the sums of the chosen elements from both arrays are equal. Two balanced ranges are considered different if they have different start or end indices, or if the elements chosen from the arrays differ at any index i within the ranges. Return the count of such balanced ranges modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: The arrays have equal positive length and contain nonnegative integers.
For each contiguous range, choose at every position either nums1 value for the first sum or nums2 value for the second sum.
Count choices whose two sums are equal, modulo 1000000007; different ranges or choices count separately.
hints: Represent choosing nums1 as a positive balance change and nums2 as a negative change.
Maintain counts of balances for ranges ending at the previous index, then start or extend ranges at the current index.
Build current from +a and -b starts plus both transitions from every prior balance; add current[0].
Each state corresponds uniquely to a range ending here and its choices, so zero balance counts exactly the new balanced ranges.

tests.explanation: Exactly three range-and-choice combinations balance the two selected sums.
Every nonempty range and every binary choice balances, totaling eight.
